pages.text: Grandma let the water out of the paddy. The soil began to show.
Yesterday, Dingding's footprints had sunk into the wet mud. Today, the dry ground held no footprints.
"Can I leave footprints today?" Dingding asked. Grandma let out the rest of the water.
"It needs to dry completely," Grandma said. Not a drop of water was left.
The bright sun shone down. The soil grew hard.
Cracks spread across the ground. Dingding stepped on it, but no footprint appeared.
Grandma nudged a clod with her foot. It was as hard as stone. "The sun is strong this year. The roots might get hurt."
Dingding tugged Grandma's hand. "Let's give it a little water. Just a tiny bit."
Grandma let a trickle of water in from the higher paddy. The soil softened.
Dingding left a line of footprints. Grandma made another line beside it. The two trails went on together.
